title: Callouts, named credentials, authentication, timeouts, retries, and mocking
objectives: Explain Apex HTTP/SOAP callouts and why named credentials beat hardcoded URLs and secrets.
Apply official callout governors: 100 callouts and 120 seconds cumulative timeout per transaction.
Sequence DML and callouts to avoid uncommitted-work errors and FOR UPDATE lock release (APEX-010).
Mock callouts in tests with HttpCalloutMock / Test.setMock rather than live endpoints.
diagnostic_question: A trigger updates LAB_Order__c then Http.sends to an allocator using a password in code. Tests hit the real network. What do you change about named credentials, transaction order, timeouts, retries, and mocking?
definition: An Apex callout is an HTTP or SOAP request from Salesforce to an external endpoint. The site must be allowed via Remote Site Settings unless you use a named credential, which stores the endpoint URL and authentication so Apex can call callout:My_Named_Credential/path without embedding secrets. Official per-transaction limits: 100 callouts and 120 seconds cumulative timeout. Tests must mock HTTP—they cannot freely call the live network. ([Invoking Callouts Using Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_callouts.htm); [Named Credentials as Callout Endpoints](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_callouts_named_credentials.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))
why_it_matters: Hardcoded passwords, callout-after-DML, and live-network tests are common interview and incident failures. Named credentials keep auth out of Apex; Queueable (APEX-011) gives the callout its own transaction.
sixty_second_explanation: Treat the integration as a bonded courier. The named credential is the passport and destination on file; Apex only says callout:LAB_Allocator/v1. You do not stuff cash (passwords) in the backpack. You get 100 stops and 120 seconds total on this trip. You cannot mix uncommitted DML then a callout in the same transaction—finish DML or move the courier to a Queueable after commit. Retries need idempotency and delay so you do not burn daily async. Tests use a dummy loading dock (HttpCalloutMock), not the real warehouse.
deeper_explanation: Callouts let Apex invoke external HTTP or SOAP services. Unauthorized addresses fail unless registered in Remote Site Settings or covered by a named credential. Apex web services are the inverse: the outside world calls in. ([Invoking Callouts Using Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_callouts.htm))

A named credential stores the endpoint URL and authentication. Salesforce applies auth so Apex does not. You skip remote site settings for that URL. Reference callout:Name/optional/path?query=. Changing the URL later does not require a code edit. The same name can point at different URLs per org for packaging. ([Named Credentials as Callout Endpoints](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_callouts_named_credentials.htm))

Governors: 100 callouts per transaction; 120 seconds cumulative timeout for all callouts in the transaction. Heap/CPU still apply. Scheduled Apex uses synchronous limits if you mistakenly callout from Schedulable.execute. ([Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

You cannot perform a callout after uncommitted DML in the same transaction (uncommitted work pending). FOR UPDATE locks are released on callout (APEX-010). Preferred sequence: compute, DML, commit, Queueable callout—or callout first then DML if the design allows. @future(callout=true) or Queueable with Database.AllowsCallouts.

Retries are application design, not a platform auto-retry of Http.send. Use Queueable delay (0–10 minutes) or a halt after N attempts. Tests: implement HttpCalloutMock and Test.setMock so tests do not depend on the network. Live callouts in tests are the wrong default.

mental_model.analogy: A bonded courier: the named credential is the passport and destination on file; Apex only hands over the sealed pouch. Timeouts are the shift clock (120 seconds total). The dummy loading dock is HttpCalloutMock.
useful_mapping: passport + destination card → named credential + external credential
cash in the backpack → password in Apex source
100 stops / 120-minute-wait clock → 100 callouts / 120 s cumulative (seconds, not minutes)
leaving the vault mid-count → callout after uncommitted DML or under FOR UPDATE
second truck tomorrow → Queueable retry with delay
where_it_breaks: The 120-second cap is cumulative seconds, not a 120-minute shift.
Named credentials do not make a non-idempotent POST safe to retry.
Continuations for long Visualforce/LWC callouts are a neighboring pattern, not this lesson's default.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Callouts are HTTP/SOAP from Apex. Use a named credential and callout:Name so secrets stay out of code. 100 callouts and 120 seconds cumulative per transaction. Do not callout after uncommitted DML; use Queueable after commit. Tests use HttpCalloutMock.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I refuse passwords in custom metadata used as a hiding place if a named credential fits. I sequence callout-before-DML or DML-commit-then-Queueable. I set request timeouts consciously and still respect the 120 s cumulative cap. Retries are idempotent Queueable delays, not a for-loop of Http.send. I implement HttpCalloutMock and Test.setMock. I cite Execution Governors and Limits, not a blog's 10-callout myth.

terminology.plain: Apex calling an external HTTP or SOAP service.
terminology.precise: Http.send or generated SOAP from a WSDL. Requires remote site or named credential.
terminology.non_example: A platform event publish is not an HTTP callout.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Inbound REST Apex: the inverse direction.

terminology.precise: Setup definition; Apex uses callout:Name/path; Salesforce injects auth; remote site not required for that URL.
terminology.non_example: String password in an Apex constant.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Remote site setting: allowlist only, no auth vault.
terminology.boundary: Same name, different URL per org for packaging.

terminology.plain: Proving the call is allowed to the external system.
terminology.precise: Managed by the named/external credential (OAuth, named principal, etc.). Apex should not assemble Bearer tokens from secrets in source.
terminology.example: External credential OAuth 2.0 client credentials for LAB_Allocator.
terminology.non_example: Checking a Salesforce profile (that is org authorization, APEX-015).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Remote site: network allow, not OAuth.
terminology.boundary: Reverify protocol options in current Help.

terminology.plain: How long this request may wait.
terminology.precise: HttpRequest supports read/connection timeouts; all callouts in the transaction share a 120-second cumulative governor.
terminology.example: req.setTimeout(20000) still counts toward 120 s total.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lock wait 10 s (APEX-010) is not a callout timeout.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent the default if unset—read HTTP Classes.

terminology.plain: Trying the external call again after a transient failure.
terminology.precise: Not automatic on Http.send. Use Queueable delay and idempotency. Halt on 4xx poison messages.
terminology.example: Re-enqueue LAB_AllocQueueable with delay 5 after HTTP 503.
terminology.non_example: for-loop of 100 Http.send in a trigger.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Daily async: retries consume Queueable executions.
terminology.boundary: Without idempotency keys you may double-charge.

terminology.precise: HttpCalloutMock + Test.setMock so assertions do not need the allocator to be up.
terminology.example: Mock returns 200 and a LAB_ JSON body.
terminology.boundary: APEX-016 owns startTest; this lesson owns the mock.

terminology.precise: Required when the callout does not use a named credential. Unauthorized addresses fail.
terminology.example: Legacy endpoint still on a remote site.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: CSP trusted sites for LWC are not Apex callouts.
terminology.boundary: Prefer named credentials for new work.

terminology.plain: DML not yet committed when you try to callout.
terminology.precise: The platform blocks callout-after-DML in the same transaction. Split with async or reorder.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Publish Immediately is not a callout.
terminology.boundary: FOR UPDATE locks also drop on callout.

when_to_use: When Apex must HTTP or SOAP to an external system: use a callout with a named credential, not a password in source.
When the endpoint or authentication differs by org: same named credential name, different URL.
When DML already happened: move the callout to Queueable after commit (timeouts and retries live there).
When writing tests: HttpCalloutMock mocking, never a live allocator dependency.
When the external API is rate-limited: Queueable delay rather than a tight retry loop that burns 100 callouts.
When you must cite 100 callouts and 120 seconds cumulative from Execution Governors and Limits.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a synchronous trigger callout after DML; that trips uncommitted work and can release FOR UPDATE locks.
Do not use Remote Site Settings plus hardcoded OAuth as the default when a named credential fits.
Do not retry non-idempotent POSTs in a for-loop of Http.send.
Do not skip mocking because 'the sandbox can reach QA.'
Do not invent a 10-callout myth; the governors page says 100.
Do not put callouts in Schedulable.execute expecting async CPU—scheduled jobs use sync limits (APEX-011).
configuration_or_code_location: Setup → Remote Site Settings only for legacy raw URLs.

interview_questions.question: How do you authenticate an Apex callout in 2026?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Named credential plus external credential. Apex only uses callout:Name/path. Salesforce injects authentication. I do not put passwords in classes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I contrast remote-site-plus-header hacks. I mention packaging: same name, different URL per org. I still enforce HTTPS and least-privilege named principals. I will reverify the exact OAuth click-path in Help rather than inventing Setup labels.
follow_ups: Can you merge fields in headers?
weak_answer_warnings: Pasting a bearer token into Apex

interview_questions.question: What official callout limits do you cite?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: 100 callouts and 120 seconds cumulative per transaction from Execution Governors and Limits. I will not quote a 10-callout myth.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add that CPU/heap still apply and scheduled Apex uses sync limits. I setTimeout on the request but know it still counts toward 120 s. High volume goes to Queueable/Batch, not a trigger loop. I reverify the table for the class API version.
interview_questions.example: A trigger looping Http.send over 200 orders blows 100 quickly.

interview_questions.question: Trigger inserts an order then callouts. It fails. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Uncommitted work pending: no callout after uncommitted DML. Also, a FOR UPDATE before the callout would already be released.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I move the callout to Queueable after commit, or callout-then-DML if the vendor reservation must precede the insert. I add a mock test for both success and 500. I do not catch the exception and retry Http.send in the trigger.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Order after-insert Http.send to allocator → uncommitted work error.

interview_questions.question: How do you test the allocator callout?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: HttpCalloutMock returns canned 200/500 bodies. Test.setMock before invoking the service. startTest/stopTest if the service is Queueable. No live URL.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I assert status mapping and that a 500 writes a LAB_ error, not that the vendor is up. I never SeeAllData to steal a production named credential. APEX-016 owns isolation; this lesson owns the mock interface.
tradeoffs: One mock vs several status cases
Static resource mock vs inner class
follow_ups: Can tests do real callouts at all?
What exception if mock is missing?
weak_answer_warnings: Hitting QA from a unit test

interview_questions.question: How do you retry a failed callout without a storm?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Queueable delay, idempotency key, halt after N attempts. I do not for-loop Http.send up to 100. 4xx poison messages stop; 503 may retry once.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The Queueable page warns that delay 0 plus chaining burns daily async. I store a LAB_Attempt__c count. I never retry a non-idempotent charge POST without the vendor's idempotency header. Timeouts still count toward 120 s in each transaction, but each Queueable is a new transaction.
interview_questions.example: LAB_AllocQueueable on 503 enqueues itself with delay 5 minutes if attempts < 2.
follow_ups: Does rollback cancel the retry job?

interview_questions.question: Unauthorized endpoint in a sandbox. Walk it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check the named credential name in setEndpoint, then remote site if it is a raw URL. Do not rotate passwords first.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare callout:LAB_Allocator versus a typo. I confirm the named credential exists in this org. For packaged code I expect the name to match and the URL to differ. I look at debug for the exact host. I still do not log the Authorization header.
follow_ups: How do you test without the NC?
weak_answer_warnings: Pasting the token into the request to 'just see'

interview_questions.question: Callout plus FOR UPDATE in one design. What is the safe sequence?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Do not lock then callout. Callouts release FOR UPDATE locks. Lock, DML, commit, then Queueable callout—or callout first if the vendor must reserve before Salesforce DML.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I connect APEX-010 and this topic. I show FOR_UPDATE_LOCKS_RELEASE in a debug log as evidence. I refuse Http.send in the critical section. If the vendor needs the Salesforce Id, I must DML first, which forces async callout.
interview_questions.example: Inventory FOR UPDATE, decrement, update, enqueue LAB_AllocQueueable.
follow_ups: Can you callout in before trigger?
weak_answer_warnings: Claiming named credentials keep the lock

interview_questions.question: When is a callout the wrong tool?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When a platform event or CDC already fans out to the ERP, or when before-save Flow can stay in-org. Callouts are for request/response to a system that is not on the event bus.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I will not Http.send from a 200-row trigger. I will not use callouts as a database. I mention 100/120 s and daily async if we Queueable every row. Sometimes inbound REST (the inverse) is the better contract. I do not invent timeout numbers beyond the governors table.
interview_questions.example: ERP already subscribed to LAB_Shipment__ChangeEvent: no per-row callout from the writer.
